facts.raw_span: multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
The lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size since age 24
had been bleeding occasionally after trauma
right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
recurrent seizures at age 4
lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity
had been wearing compression stockings for years
family history revealed similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography: Demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm

Biopsy revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis
Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

The patient's presentation of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, along with sonography and histopathology results, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's presentation of lipolymphedema of the lower legs, attributed to functional venous insufficiency, supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules are characteristic of cutaneous venous malformations and cerebral cavernous malformations.
rationales.F04: Right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage suggest a possible cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F06: Lipolymphedema of the lower legs is a distinct condition but may be related to venous insufficiency.
rationales.F08: Family history of similar conditions suggests a possible genetic component, such as familial cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F09: Father's death from an intracranial hemorrhage supports the possibility of a hereditary condition like familial cerebral cavernous malformation.
rationales.F11: Histopathology results showing dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle are consistent with cerebral cavernous malformations and cutaneous venous malformations.
rationales.F12: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant is a strong indicator of cerebral cavernous malformation.
